UnitStatement: The development plan connects governed AI agents, deterministic engineering engines, local project truth, professional review, and external validation tools.
The plan treats Chirality App and OpenPipeStress as parts of a larger professional-engineering software ecosystem.
The ecosystem is a layered system rather than a single monolithic application.
Chirality App is the governed professional-work harness and agent operating layer.
The Domain Engine Framework supplies the profile, tool-adapter, artifact, write-boundary, and operation-proposal layer.
OpenPipeStress is the first deterministic domain engine for piping design, model authoring, and stress-analysis core work.
External Professional Prover Tools are industry-accepted validation tools used outside the design engine.
The Human Professional or Responsible Reviewer is the final authority for project reliance.
Agents propose and organize while domain engines compute, external tools validate, humans accept, and git-tracked files remember.
Chirality should become the governed operating layer for many deterministic professional domain engines, not only piping stress analysis.
Professional AI systems should coordinate deterministic engineering engines and professional judgment rather than replace them.
The combined system should make professional work faster and more traceable.
Project truth should live in local, versioned files.
Domain truth should live in deterministic domain engines.
Agents should operate through explicit scopes, tools, proposals, and manifests.
Unknowns should become TBD entries rather than guesses.
Computations should come from deterministic tools rather than agent improvisation.
Professional reliance remains a human and project-authority act.
External prover tools remain authoritative where the industry requires them.
The OpenPipeStress workflow moves from design basis through model and analysis artifacts to external validation, human interpretation, revision, comparison, and reporting.
The Chirality workflow moves from scope through packages, dependencies, agent work, tool outputs, review, gates, and a git-tracked project record.
The ecosystem works when the Chirality and OpenPipeStress chains connect through files, manifests, adapters, and human-gated operations.
Chirality is responsible for working-root selection.
Chirality is responsible for project scaffolding.
Chirality is responsible for agent orchestration.
Chirality is responsible for package and deliverable structure.
Chirality is responsible for dependency registers.
Chirality is responsible for lifecycle records.
Chirality is responsible for review notes.
Chirality is responsible for assumption and TBD registers.
Chirality is responsible for deterministic tool invocation.
Chirality is responsible for generated summaries and report drafts.
Chirality is responsible for human gate support.
Chirality is responsible for git-trackable project memory.
Chirality is not responsible for solving piping stress models.
Chirality is not responsible for owning the OpenPipeStress canonical model.
Chirality is not responsible for approving engineering work.
Chirality is not responsible for declaring code compliance.
Chirality is not responsible for parsing proprietary third-party engineering results unless separately scoped.
Chirality is not responsible for replacing domain tools.
The Domain Engine Framework bridges Chirality and deterministic specialist software.
The Domain Engine Framework is responsible for the domain engine profile schema.
The Domain Engine Framework is responsible for artifact discovery.
The Domain Engine Framework is responsible for protected path declarations.
The Domain Engine Framework is responsible for agent-writable path declarations.
The Domain Engine Framework is responsible for deterministic tool adapter contracts.
The Domain Engine Framework is responsible for tool invocation logging.
The Domain Engine Framework is responsible for operation proposal schema.
The Domain Engine Framework is responsible for generated summary and manifest conventions.
The Domain Engine Framework is responsible for professional-boundary and IP/data-boundary checks.
The Domain Engine Framework is an integration contract rather than a solver or domain application.
OpenPipeStress is responsible for the schema-backed physical piping model.
OpenPipeStress is responsible for analytical model transformation.
OpenPipeStress is responsible for a full internal piping flexibility and stress analytical engine.
OpenPipeStress is responsible for 3D GUI and model editing.
OpenPipeStress is responsible for model states.
OpenPipeStress is responsible for analysis runs.
OpenPipeStress is responsible for generic model-state and analysis-run comparisons.
OpenPipeStress is responsible for rule-pack evaluation using user-supplied data.
OpenPipeStress is responsible for handoff packages.
OpenPipeStress is responsible for deterministic summaries and reports.
OpenPipeStress is responsible for operation proposal validation.
OpenPipeStress is responsible for professional and IP/data boundary notices.
OpenPipeStress is not responsible for being a general-purpose agent operating system.
OpenPipeStress is not responsible for becoming the full deliverable-management layer for the project.
OpenPipeStress is not responsible for claiming industry-standard professional validation by itself.
OpenPipeStress is not responsible for replacing external professional stress-analysis prover tools.
OpenPipeStress is not responsible for accepting or sealing engineering work.
External professional stress-analysis tools are responsible for project validation when accepted industry software is required.
External professional stress-analysis tools are not controlled by Chirality or OpenPipeStress in the near-term MVP.
The near-term external prover workflow is human-mediated.
The near-term workflow passes an OpenPipeStress handoff package to user-driven external-tool review and back into OpenPipeStress and Chirality records.
The human professional or accountable reviewer decides what is correct for the project.
The human professional or accountable reviewer accepts or rejects agent proposals.
The human professional or accountable reviewer accepts or rejects model changes.
The human professional or accountable reviewer interprets external prover results.
The human professional or accountable reviewer issues or approves deliverables where appropriate.
The human professional or accountable reviewer ensures licensed standards, project basis, and owner requirements are applied correctly.
The program architecture layers human authority, Chirality, the Domain Engine Framework, OpenPipeStress, and external professional prover tools.
The data flow begins with Chirality creating project and deliverable structure.
OpenPipeStress creates and owns the domain model in the data flow.
OpenPipeStress generates manifests and summaries for the data flow.
Chirality agents review summaries and propose actions in the data flow.
OpenPipeStress validates proposed operations in the data flow.
The human accepts or rejects proposed changes in the data flow.
OpenPipeStress creates new model states, runs, and comparisons after accepted actions.
Chirality records review notes, TBDs, reports, and handoff checklists.
External prover validation occurs outside the Chirality and OpenPipeStress system.
The human feeds external conclusions back into the project record.
No agent should ever be the source of accepted engineering truth.
Agents may create drafts, summaries, review notes, operation proposals, TBD registers, dependency rows, handoff checklists, and report fragments.
Agents must not directly create accepted model states, solver results, professional approval, code-compliance conclusions, external-prover validation status, or signed records.
The development program should proceed in ten phases.
Each phase is a risk-management step with a distinct purpose and exit gate, not merely a feature release.
Phase 0 locks the shared vision before integration code is built.
Phase 0 produces a Chirality PRD amendment, an integration plan, this development plan, an OpenPipeStress alignment note, and a source-basis map.
Phase 0 decides that Chirality is the governed work harness.
Phase 0 decides that OpenPipeStress is the first deterministic domain engine.
Phase 0 decides that the integration is federated rather than monolithic.
Phase 0 decides that domain engines own canonical domain artifacts.
Phase 0 decides that agents create proposals and summaries rather than accepted engineering changes.
Phase 0 decides that human gates remain mandatory for reliance.
Phase 0 exits when the project owner accepts the architecture.
Phase 0 exits when the Chirality PRD amendment is adopted or marked pending adoption.
Phase 0 exits when the OpenPipeStress PRD recognizes Chirality integration as an external or domain profile pathway.
Phase 0 exits when non-goals are explicit and visible.
Phase 1 defines the general integration layer so OpenPipeStress does not become a one-off hack.
Phase 1 Chirality work creates domain-engine profile, tool-adapter, write-boundary, operation-proposal, artifact-manifest, and boundary-notice specifications.
Phase 1 OpenPipeStress work creates its Chirality profile, artifact layout, CLI adapter spec, and operation proposal schema.
A domain profile must declare authoritative artifacts, readable artifacts, protected write paths, agent-writable paths, deterministic tools, boundary phrases, and IP/data constraints.
The OpenPipeStress profile must validate against the general domain profile schema.
The profile must make clear which artifacts agents may and may not touch.
Phase 1 exits when the framework describes OpenPipeStress without embedding piping-specific logic in Chirality core.
Phase 2 builds enough OpenPipeStress core functionality for the domain engine to be real.
Phase 2 OpenPipeStress work implements project schema, units, physical and analytical models, piping elements, supports, loads, solver, stress recovery, diagnostics, and local storage.
During Phase 2, Chirality may only store planning artifacts and review notes.
Phase 2 acceptance requires OpenPipeStress to solve benchmark models deterministically.
Phase 2 acceptance requires schema round-trips without data loss.
Phase 2 acceptance requires solver results to bind to explicit model inputs.
Phase 2 acceptance requires missing data and solver blockers to be visible.
Phase 2 acceptance requires no protected standards data to be bundled.
Phase 2 exits when OpenPipeStress has a credible deterministic core before Chirality agents reason around it.
Phase 3 makes OpenPipeStress outputs auditable, repeatable, and comparable.
Phase 3 OpenPipeStress work implements named immutable model states, analysis runs, metadata, hashes, comparisons, stable mapping, manual mapping, tolerances, and reports.
Phase 3 Chirality work prepares read-only consumption of model manifests, run summaries, comparison summaries, deltas, warnings, and assumption registers.
Phase 3 acceptance requires reproducible run metadata for the same state, solver version, and settings.
Phase 3 acceptance requires deterministic comparison between two model states.
Phase 3 acceptance requires deterministic comparison between two analysis runs.
Phase 3 acceptance requires comparison outputs suitable for human and agent review.
Phase 3 acceptance requires the comparison tool not to imply external validation or professional approval.
Phase 3 exits when the domain engine generates core artifacts that Chirality agents can safely summarize and reason about.
Phase 4 lets Chirality discover and read OpenPipeStress artifacts without writing domain truth.
Phase 4 Chirality work implements domain profile loading, validation, artifact scanning, protected path recognition, read-only tool registry, UI display, and context injection.
Phase 4 OpenPipeStress work implements read-only adapter commands for validation, summaries, state/run/comparison listing, and boundary checks.
Phase 4 acceptance requires Chirality to detect an OpenPipeStress project inside a working root.
Phase 4 acceptance requires Chirality to show model states, runs, comparisons, warnings, and manifests.
Phase 4 acceptance requires agents to summarize actual OpenPipeStress-generated summaries.
Phase 4 acceptance requires agents to be unable to write protected domain artifacts directly.
Phase 4 acceptance requires Chirality to report missing or invalid OpenPipeStress without pretending to know domain state.
Phase 4 exits when Chirality can support OpenPipeStress review workflows without changing the engineering model.
Phase 5 allows Chirality to request deterministic OpenPipeStress outputs through approved tools.
Phase 5 Chirality work implements domain tool invocation, argument validation, output capture, logging, high-impact confirmations, and result indexing.
Phase 5 OpenPipeStress work implements write-producing adapter commands for analysis, state comparison, run comparison, handoff, and report fragments.
Phase 5 write-producing adapter commands are domain-controlled writes, not agent writes.
Phase 5 acceptance requires a user to trigger an OpenPipeStress analysis run through Chirality.
Phase 5 acceptance requires OpenPipeStress, not an agent, to create run records.
Phase 5 acceptance requires a user to trigger comparison generation through Chirality.
Phase 5 acceptance requires OpenPipeStress to create comparison records and delta tables.
Phase 5 acceptance requires a user to generate a handoff package.
Phase 5 acceptance requires Chirality to record summaries and checklist artifacts.
Phase 5 acceptance requires protected canonical domain files to remain controlled by OpenPipeStress.
Phase 5 exits when Chirality can orchestrate deterministic domain work while preserving domain ownership.
Phase 6 lets agents become useful design assistants without allowing direct model mutation.
Phase 6 Chirality work implements proposal templates, authoring support, proposal browser, review-note linkage, TBD extraction, and proposal lifecycle metadata.
Phase 6 OpenPipeStress work implements operation proposal validation, schema validation, diff preview, warnings, blockers, and rationale capture.
Future Phase 6 OpenPipeStress work applies operation proposals with human approval, new model states, and operation application records.
Phase 6 acceptance requires agents to draft operation proposals.
Phase 6 acceptance requires OpenPipeStress to validate proposals without mutating the model.
Phase 6 acceptance requires users to inspect proposed changes and blockers.
Phase 6 acceptance requires invalid proposals not to become model changes.
Phase 6 acceptance requires accepted changes to create new model states through OpenPipeStress only.
Phase 6 acceptance requires agent output to be clearly marked proposal-only.
Phase 6 exits when agents can participate in design iteration safely.
Phase 7 makes the human workflow smooth across OpenPipeStress and Chirality.
Phase 7 OpenPipeStress work implements or matures GUI editing, model tree, inspector, history, browsers, panels, proposal review UI, and handoff UI.
Phase 7 Chirality work implements open-in-domain-app actions, deep links, dashboard, proposal list, review-note generation, and deliverable package generation.
Phase 7 acceptance requires users to review issues in Chirality, work in OpenPipeStress, compare before and after, and update review notes and deliverables.
Phase 7 exits when the integrated workflow feels like one governed professional process while the applications remain distinct.
Phase 8 supports the real professional validation workflow without overbuilding proprietary integrations too early.
Phase 8 OpenPipeStress work implements handoff packages, units, IDs, load cases, supports, warnings, assumptions, target mapping, and unsupported-behavior flags.
Phase 8 Chirality work implements handoff checklists, external review TBD registers, comment intake, change-record scaffolding, and post-review comparison summaries.
Phase 8 workflow moves from an OpenPipeStress handoff package to Chirality checklist, external tool use, comments, TBDs/proposals, model revision, comparison, and outcome records.
Phase 8 acceptance requires no automatic claim of external validation.
Phase 8 acceptance requires the user to record external review comments.
Phase 8 acceptance requires Chirality to organize external-review-driven changes.
Phase 8 acceptance requires OpenPipeStress to compare pre-review and post-review model states.
Phase 8 acceptance requires reports to distinguish internal analysis from external review and human acceptance.
Phase 8 exits when the workflow supports engineering practice without pretending to automate professional reliance.
Phase 9 makes Domain Engine Integration reusable for future professional tools.
Phase 9 abstracts profile registry, dashboard, adapter invocation, scanner, proposal UI, protected path guard, and boundary notice framework.
Candidate future domain engines include structural frame analysis, electrical load-flow, process simulation, cost estimating, scheduling/risk, compliance checking, and inspection planning.
Phase 9 acceptance requires a second domain engine profile without modifying core Chirality logic.
Phase 9 acceptance requires domain tools to be listed, invoked, and summarized generically.
Phase 9 acceptance requires professional-boundary and protected-write behavior across all domain engines.
Phase 9 exits when Chirality is a governed professional-work harness for deterministic domain engines.
Phase 10 uses agents to coordinate across multiple deterministic engines and deliverable packages.

Phase 10 capabilities include cross-domain dependencies, impact analysis, change propagation, change packages, risk/TBD heat maps, readiness scoring, scenario proposals, dashboards, and external result states.
Even in Phase 10, agents remain coordinators and proposal generators rather than approving authorities.
Phase 10 acceptance requires agents to identify cross-domain impacts using deterministic artifacts.
Phase 10 acceptance requires users to see affected deliverables, model states, and handoff packages.
Phase 10 acceptance requires change management without automatic professional acceptance.
The program should be managed through parallel but coordinated workstreams.
Workstream A ensures Chirality is reliable enough to be the professional-work harness.

Workstream A key work covers context composition, working-root validation, persistence, SSE stability, attachment policy, runtime options, tool registry, lifecycle, dependencies, audit behavior, typed errors, and packaging.
Workstream A must close the provider-turn gap in composing selected agent instructions and working-root governance context into the live provider path.
Workstream A is done when agent turns are governed by the correct persona and project context.
Workstream A is done when deterministic tools are callable and logged.
Workstream A is done when project truth remains in working-root files.
Workstream A is done when human-gate posture remains visible.
Workstream B builds the reusable Domain Engine Framework integration layer.
Workstream B key work includes profile schemas, validation, artifact scanning, protected and writable paths, tool registry, output capture, operation proposals, notices, and fixture tests.
Workstream B is done when OpenPipeStress can be integrated through a profile.
Workstream B is done when Chirality can support one additional hypothetical profile without major redesign.
Workstream B is done when agents cannot write protected domain artifacts through supported write paths.
Workstream C builds the deterministic engineering engine.
Workstream C key work includes schema, units, models, solver, loads, supports, stress recovery, states, runs, comparison, reports, handoff, GUI, rule packs, libraries, and validation.
Workstream C is done when OpenPipeStress can model, solve, save, compare, and export a small meaningful piping design case.
Workstream C is done when OpenPipeStress outputs are deterministic and auditable.
Workstream C is done when protected standards content is not shipped.
Workstream D exposes OpenPipeStress safely to Chirality.
Workstream D key work includes CLI adapter, read-only commands, write-producing domain commands, summaries, manifests, proposal validation, report fragments, and boundary checks.
Workstream D is done when Chirality can call OpenPipeStress tools without directly editing canonical model files.
Workstream D is done when tool outputs are bounded and suitable for agent context.
Workstream D is done when adapter commands have schemas, tests, and deterministic outputs.
Workstream E prevents the ecosystem from making unsafe or legally risky claims.
Workstream E key work includes boundary notices, report and agent language checks, private data checks, quarantine, contribution review, public/private separation, and provenance fields.
Workstream E is done when reports and agent outputs do not imply professional acceptance.
Workstream E is done when public artifacts do not contain protected standards data.
Workstream E is done when private rule packs and project data are excluded from public outputs by default.
Workstream F creates proof that the ecosystem works.
Demo Project 1 uses a small L-bend or U-loop model with two states, two runs, one comparison, one handoff manifest, and one Chirality review package.
Demo Project 2 covers external review feedback through comments, agent operation proposal, user-applied change, new run, comparison summary, and handoff update.
Demo Project 3 defines a mock second domain engine with profile-only integration, read-only summaries, protected paths, and operation proposal fixture.
Workstream F is done when fixture projects let a new user understand the whole system.
Workstream F is done when tests prove agents do not directly write protected domain files.
Workstream F is done when the demo demonstrates the big-picture architecture.
The release roadmap describes integrated program releases rather than only individual app versions.
Program Release 0 uses Chirality and OpenPipeStress side by side without code integration.
Program Release 0 includes the plan documents, working-root layout, manual artifact guidance, review-note templates, TBD templates, and handoff templates.
Program Release 0 succeeds when a user manually exports OpenPipeStress artifacts and uses Chirality agents to organize review work.
Program Release 1 lets Chirality discover and summarize OpenPipeStress projects.
Program Release 1 includes profile schema, OpenPipeStress profile, validation, artifact scanner, validation command, summary command, and state/run listing commands.
Program Release 1 succeeds when agents read actual OpenPipeStress summaries and produce review notes without editing model truth.
Program Release 2 lets Chirality request or consume OpenPipeStress states, runs, and comparisons.
Program Release 2 includes analysis runs, state comparison, run comparison, tool output capture, comparison summaries, delta tables, and protected path guard.
Program Release 2 succeeds when users compare states or runs and Chirality summarizes the result.
Program Release 3 supports the external prover workflow.
Program Release 3 includes handoff generation, handoff manifest, export warnings, external review TBD register, handoff checklist, and comment intake.
Program Release 3 succeeds when a user prepares a professional-tool handoff package and maintains a clear Chirality review record.
Program Release 4 lets agents propose model changes safely.
Program Release 4 includes operation proposal schema, templates, validation command, diff preview, proposal browser, and review-note linkage.
Program Release 4 succeeds when an agent proposes a support or route change, OpenPipeStress validates it, and the user decides whether to apply it.
Program Release 5 applies validated proposals through OpenPipeStress with human approval.
Program Release 5 includes operation proposal application, approval reference capture, new model state creation, application record, and proposal review UI.
Program Release 5 succeeds when an accepted proposal creates a new OpenPipeStress model state through the domain engine rather than raw agent mutation.
Program Release 6 makes the integration reusable beyond OpenPipeStress.
Program Release 6 includes a domain engine starter kit, profile examples, adapter templates, fixture domain engine, documentation, and test harness.
Program Release 6 succeeds when a second deterministic domain engine can integrate with Chirality using the same pattern.
Program Release 7 coordinates multiple domain engines and deliverables.
Program Release 7 includes cross-domain dependency tracking, impact analysis, dashboard, risk/TBD heat map, and multi-engine handoff packages.
Program Release 7 succeeds when Chirality becomes a governed professional-work operating layer across multiple deterministic tools.

The first meaningful integrated MVP includes Chirality domain profile validation, artifact scanning, protected path recognition, read-only tool invocation, summary access, and review/TBD/report generation.
The first meaningful integrated MVP includes OpenPipeStress schema, small model solving, model states, analysis runs, summaries, comparisons, handoff manifest skeleton, and read-only CLI adapter.
The first meaningful integrated MVP includes shared profile, working-root layout, fixture project, professional-boundary notices, and IP/data-boundary notices.
The MVP excludes direct agent editing of OpenPipeStress models.
The MVP excludes external commercial software output parsers.
The MVP excludes automatic external validation status.
The MVP excludes automatic professional approval.
The MVP excludes full dynamic analysis.
The MVP excludes full CAD/BIM integration.
The MVP excludes full route optimization.
The integration should use files and manifests as the shared boundary.
Filesystem boundary use aligns with the Chirality project-truth model.
Filesystem boundary use preserves local-first operation.
Filesystem boundary use supports git diff, audit, rollback, and human review.
Filesystem boundary use avoids hidden database state.
Filesystem boundary use allows domain engines to retain their internal schemas.
OpenPipeStress should expose a CLI or equivalent deterministic adapter before deep UI integration.
A CLI or tool adapter is easier to test, invoke, log, and keep deterministic than GUI automation.
The domain profile must declare protected paths.
Protected paths prevent raw agent mutation of accepted model truth.
Protected paths make safety visible.
Protected paths support testable guardrails.
Protected paths preserve domain-engine ownership.
OpenPipeStress should produce bounded summaries for Chirality agents.
Bounded summaries are needed because agents cannot safely read unlimited model or result internals.
Generated summaries reduce context overload.
Generated manifests allow traceability.
Warnings and TBDs become easier to organize through generated summaries and manifests.
Agents should propose changes as structured data.
Structured operation proposals can be validated before application.
Structured operation proposals let users inspect diffs.
Structured operation proposals allow invalid or unsafe proposals to be rejected.
Applied structured proposals can create traceable new model states.
The Chirality backlog includes domain profiles, validation, scanning, protected path guard, tool registry, invocation API, output capture, proposals, dashboard, notices, and fixture tests.

The OpenPipeStress backlog includes canonical schema, units, physical model, analytical transform, solver, stress recovery, states, runs, comparisons, handoff, CLI, summaries, boundary checks, proposals, and GUI.
The shared backlog includes OpenPipeStress domain profile, working-root fixture, demo script, boundary tests, protected path tests, handoff checklist template, and external review workflow.

Chirality tests cover profile validation and discovery, invalid profile rejection, path matching, artifact scanning, invocation validation, output capture, failure behavior, missing engine behavior, and write rejection.

OpenPipeStress tests cover schema round-trip, unit conversion, solver benchmarks, state hashing, run reproducibility, comparisons, handoff completeness, summaries, proposal validation, redaction, and notices.
Integration tests cover project scanning, profile validation, model summaries, agent review notes, analysis runs, comparison deltas, handoff generation, and protected path enforcement.
Governance tests cover approval and compliance claims, required notices, protected content flagging, private rule-pack leakage, and fabricated external prover status.
The first end-to-end demonstration should be deliberately small.
The demonstration scenario uses a simple piping route with an anchor, elbow, support, and thermal load.
The demonstration flow moves through Chirality scaffolding, OpenPipeStress states and runs, agent summaries, model revision, comparison, handoff manifest, and handoff checklist.
The demonstration succeeds when results come from OpenPipeStress rather than the agent.
The demonstration succeeds when review notes come from Chirality agents rather than the solver.
The demonstration succeeds when model changes occur through OpenPipeStress rather than raw agent edits.
The demonstration succeeds when files are local and git-trackable.
The demonstration succeeds when no professional approval is implied.
A key risk is Chirality becoming too domain-specific; the mitigation is a generic Domain Engine Profile with OpenPipeStress as the first profile.
A key risk is agents mutating engineering model truth; mitigation uses protected paths, write guards, operation proposals, and domain-controlled tools.
A key risk is OpenPipeStress becoming an agent OS; mitigation keeps it focused on model, GUI, solver, states, runs, comparison, and handoff.
A key risk is agent summaries fabricating engineering conclusions; mitigation requires deterministic tool outputs, manifests, IDs, and boundary notices.
A key risk is users mistaking internal results for professional validation; mitigation uses notices, boundary policy, and no automatic approval or compliance statuses.
A key risk is overbuilding the external prover workflow too early; mitigation starts with handoff manifest and user-mediated feedback.
A key risk is private or protected data leaking into public artifacts; mitigation uses IP/data checks, redaction, private-by-default paths, and provenance.
A key risk is rigid domain profiles; mitigation versions the profile schema and allows domain-specific extensions.
A key risk is integration delaying OpenPipeStress solver work; mitigation builds the OpenPipeStress core first.
A key risk is integration delaying Chirality core hardening; mitigation stages the Domain Engine Framework after core harness stability.
Gate 1 asks whether the federated Chirality, Domain Engine, and OpenPipeStress architecture is accepted.
Gate 1 requires accepted PRD amendment, accepted integration plan, and understood protected boundaries.
Gate 2 asks whether OpenPipeStress is deterministic enough to expose to agents.
Gate 2 requires solver benchmarks, schema round-trip tests, states/runs implementation, and summary generator implementation.
Gate 3 asks whether Chirality can read OpenPipeStress outputs without risking model mutation.
Gate 3 requires domain profile validation, artifact scanner, read-only adapter commands, and protected path tests.
Gate 4 asks whether Chirality can request domain-generated outputs without agents writing protected files.
Gate 4 requires tool invocation logs, output capture, domain-controlled write tests, and human confirmation for high-impact commands.
Gate 5 asks whether agents can propose changes without users mistaking proposals for accepted engineering work.
Gate 5 requires proposal schema, proposal validation, proposal labels, diff preview, and user acceptance path.
Gate 6 asks whether the handoff workflow reduces rework and improves external validation readiness.
Gate 6 requires handoff manifest completeness, external review checklist, post-review comparison workflow, and user feedback.

The documentation plan produces or updates domain-engine, tool-adapter, write-boundary, operation-proposal, OpenPipeStress profile, adapter, user guide, handoff, proposal, professional-boundary, and IP/data-boundary documents.
Platform metrics include domain profile count, registered deterministic tools, blocked protected path write attempts, generated manifests/summaries, successful tool invocations, and onboarding time.
OpenPipeStress metrics include solver benchmarks passed, schema round-trip rate, analysis-run reproducibility, comparison determinism, handoff completeness, and unresolved critical solver defects.
Workflow metrics include model-to-summary time, comparison-to-review-note time, run-to-handoff-checklist time, TBDs resolved, external-review changes traced, and proposal decisions.
Governance metrics include professional-boundary violations, private-data leaks, protected-content quarantine events, required-notice reports, and agent outputs with deterministic evidence.
The long-term product is not AI that does engineering.
The long-term product is a local-first professional engineering operating environment around deterministic domain engines, governed agents, human authority, and git-tracked records.

OpenPipeStress is the first example because piping stress analysis has engineering consequences, deterministic mechanics, rich state, boundaries, external tools, rapid iteration, and traceable assumptions.
If the pattern works for OpenPipeStress, it can generalize to other professional domains.
Near-term actions start by adopting the Chirality PRD amendment for Domain Engine Integration.
Near-term actions include creating formal Domain Engine Profile and OpenPipeStress domain profile specifications.
Near-term actions include building the OpenPipeStress core schema and read-only summary generator.
Near-term actions include building Chirality profile validation and artifact scanning.
Near-term actions include protected path guard tests and a small OpenPipeStress fixture project.
Near-term actions include read-only model review, state/run/comparison generation, handoff manifest generation, and operation proposal workflow.
Near-term actions defer external prover parsers and automatic validation statuses.
The guiding statement keeps each role honest: Chirality governs work, agents propose, OpenPipeStress computes, external tools validate, humans accept, and the filesystem remembers.
